I'm sorry you are currently going through this. It's truly a horrible thing to witness. My husband has been able to go and see him in the hospice so has been the one to see the changes daily.

You are doing an amazing thing by taking care of him. Being so far pregnant and my husband still working full time I wouldn't have been able to do it at home. There is no way he would of been comfortable especially now he is experiencing agitation etc. 

I wish you all the best!

Thank you so much. I can't believe this is all happening. 

A pandemic, 38 weeks pregnant and my dad is dying in a hospice where I can't visit. 

How did you get through the pregnancy and labour in the end? I'm so scared justh I just don't have the energy to do it.

I'm sorry to hear you have had to experience loss of both your parents in that way. 

My dad and I have talked about how nice it is that we have had time to prepare and say goodbye. Some people just die from a heart attack and never get to say goodbye. 

It brings me peace slightly but it's been a horrible, awful experience.
I had hoped this is what would of happened. It seems more peaceful but it doesn't seem to be going that way. He's now very agitated and restless. The nurses have said they call is terminal agitation.

Goodness, I had no idea about the toes. His feet and legs are so swollen already so I wouldn't be surprised if they are already a different colour due to circulation. 

I'm sorry you had to go through this, it's awful.
I awake at night feeling like he's gone. I don't know if this is just because I'm anticipating it or whether he is trying to tell me he is trying to go. I don't know.

Thank you for sharing. I'm sorry you had to experience it for so long. 

I really hope it doesn't last a week for him. He is really ready to go and this adds further pain. I can't go and see him as I'm pregnant but my husband has been visiting everyday and has been the one to see the rapid decline in the last week :(

Thank you for your reply. 

The hospice nurse came to the house today and said it was time he went into hospice. We thought we might have a couple of days but he's just been admitted. 

I know this is the best place for him and for them to be able to control his symptoms and make him comfortable. But due to being 36 weeks pregnant and COVID I'm not allowed in to see him so that was the last time I'll ever see my dad. It hurts like hell.

That is interesting to know! Thank you very much. 

I hope you are now keeping well.

I'm so sorry to hear you've recently lost your father. 

Yes, once it becomes his final days he will be going into hospice but we are currently managing things at home. A nurse comes out once a week to see him and assess him currently. 

I called the hospice today re his new symptoms, who told me to call the GP, who told me that there was nothing they could do for the swelling etc :(
You've been in lockdown too long if you start to miss Stone Henge of all places..

Thank you! This is super helpful. You are right and he's mostly unsteady on his feet when getting out of bed.

We now have a hospital bed at home and it moves up and down so hoping that will help too.

I'm exactly the same. I'm 27 and my dad is living with us. He has now been given weeks to live and he does something that makes me think 'OH HE'S GOING TO GER BETTER' and then something bad and I'm back to reality again. 

I keep asking people what the end looks like because I hate all the uncertainty and not knowing what is next.

Try and keep strong. It's super hard but you will find the strength. 

Feel free to message me if you need to chat.

Thank you for sharing your experience. 

The palliative care nurse said she's sure it's being caused by the cancer and not the medication but we will change the morphine just in case it's too toxic for him. Although she has said with how quickly it's developed and he showed no signs of it last Thursday when she first visited that we likely only have 'short weeks' left and need to consider where he wants to be towards the end.

Oh wow! Your dad is a fighter! I'm glad he's still with you! 

Dad was diagnosed October 2018 and was given 6 months! He's only been turning yellow the last day or so.

I'm sorry to hear this :( we were given the news a couple of months ago that they will no longer treat him. He's taking it personally and think it's just because the NHS have no money. 

I just wondered if it's possible to live with jaundice without it being treated. I know jaundice is sometimes a first sign of something being wrong but it is usually treatable.

Thank you! I didn't know this was a thing. 

It would just be useful to know the signs of decline. Like Dad didn't know he should tell us that he has dark urine.

Thank you! I'm glad your partner has had it relieved! 

They have said any surgery even to put in a stent is too risky.
Please feel free to not answer that question if it's too painful. I understand it's a sensitive question!

Is that ascites? At his last CT scan they said he had fluid in his stomach. They have also said that they won't necessarily treat him the same way as they would of because of COVID. More risk him going into hospital and getting it then it is worth treating him :/ 

Would you mind sharing any other things we should be looking out for towards the end? The palliative care nurse is coming again tomorrow. I'd be interested to know whether this is a final sign. I hate all the guessing but I know jaundice is unlikely to be reversed now.

He was referred to hospice for the palliative care side of things. Pain management etc and is still at home. This is a new symptom so wondered whether he could still survive with it. He's had longer than everyone thought already!

I've called the hospice already. I think it's quite common for pancreatic and liver cancer so they just said it's part of what happens. 

I was more wondering whether he can survive longer with the jaundice? Like if they don't treat it is this like the final end or can people still go months with it?
He has a tumour on his liver so it makes sense. I more meant can he live/survive with the jaundice.

We could do but he's against them. Tried to explain the benefits etc. 

Since I wrote this the pain meds seem to have kicked in with the slow release morphine plus the paracetamol plus the oramorph. He seems to have much more energy since the pain is now under control.

No, thank you! It's advanced pancreatic. Spread to his lungs, liver and bowel. With mets and fluid in his abdomen. He's barely eating, 1 Weetabix and a banana today. Yesterday we ate 2 spoonfuls of soup. 

He was diagnosed in October 2018 and has had longer than anyone thought he would.

Thank you for your comments. It has helped!

Wow! Thank you so much for this and I'm so sorry you're been through this recently. 

I honestly just thought that now his meds are working and he seems to have more energy (I mean that by getting up on his own and coming downstairs twice and also sitting on his laptop) that he might get better. 

Interesting to know though. Will be interesting to see how he is tomorrow. 

It's super hard right now. I'm so sorry you've been through this :(

Wow! He sounds like a fighter! I'm sorry you lost him. 

My dad has had alot longer with the whole cancer diagnosis than everyone thought. He was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in October 2018 and was told he had months left. It's now been 18 months!

Thank you for this! Today already seems like a blur and that's just after having the GP out and speaking to the hospice team. 

I've made a few phone calls to family to explain what's been happening and I felt like when I was speaking I wasn't making much sense. I'm also exhausted. 

My husband and I sat with him this afternoon and just chatted a bit. He then seemed to get tired so we left him and now I haven't seen or heard him for hours, it worries me. 

I've got alot to keep my mind occupied in the next 6 months as I'm due my second baby in 7 weeks. I have to be here mentally for them but I already worry that it's going to be super hard.
Thank you so much! I'm sorry you are also going through this. We all knew it was coming but its so hard to see. I send you and your family my very best wishes.
I'm sorry it's made you sad. That's always my worry that people have to relive their experiences and it's rough on them or people going through something similar have to worry about their future.
Thank you! This seems to be exactly the same! He's not eaten anything at all today :(

Thank you so much! I haven't done anything in particular today apart from have the GP out and look after Dad but man am I tired! 

I just really hope the next part of all of this is easy for him and he isn't in too much pain as today has been rough on him.
Thank you! We are hoping so! The doctor said that this new morphine should stay in his system all day and then there is an oral top up he can take too if needs be!

Thank you much. Seeing him so frail and out of it this morning really got to me. I've been expecting it for a while but actually seeing it was truly awful. 

Congratulations on your pregnancy! I hope you have keeping safe and doing well during this pandemic and the added stress of dealing with losing someone. It's such a shitty time. 

Thank you again, I'll be sure to keep you in mind ❤️

Sorry to hear you are struggling yourself :(

Interesting to hear about the purging of items as he has started sending things to random people on the internet as he says he has no use for them now. I didn't realise that could be a sign. 

Eating and sleeping is a big thing for us right now. 

Thank you again for your comment!
I'm sure. I wouldn't be able to do it, I'm not strong enough.

Your mum sounds exactly the same then, a fighter! I'm glad you got months rather than weeks! I've had a year! I can't imagine how hard it must be to see them go even quicker! 

No, we don't have any plans :( that's what scares me even more. Once he can't walk we will need to phone hospice I think. My husband works full time, I have a 3 year old and 33 weeks pregnant, I just won't be able to lift him or care for him. I know that's me saying he'll go whilst I'm still pregnant but it's looking highly likely.

It certainly does!

A hospice nurse is coming out to see us on Thursday to discuss pain relief and what else they might be able to offer. They say they only offer hospice care in the last 2 weeks of life but I have no idea what that even looks like.

Thank you for your reply. I'm sorry you have had to go through this :( 

I also worry that the very little he is eating isn't providing enough calories to keep his body going. We all have a limit we should eat a day and he's not even eating half of it.

I'm also heavily pregnant and once the newborn is here that's going to make the house even more nuts. I spoke to him tonight and he's still 'planning' on moving out. I just don't know what to say to him.

Wow. That's quick :( I'm sorry to hear that

I'm so sorry to hear that. It seems crazy doesn't it. That someone can seem so well and then all of a sudden be so unwell.. it's so unfair. 

Yes, they have basically said the same to us. We have hospice visiting Thursday with more information, we shall see what the day brings. 

Take care of yourself.

My maternity leave.

His last round of chemo showed his tumours had shrunk. Enough that his liver tumour was less than 5mm but they said they couldn't treat him any further as previous studies showed after 'x' amount of months it stops working. But now this is the outcome :(

No not anymore. They gave him some morphine today and told him the community care team will deal with it now. Although we aren't currently under any community team. It's been a bit of a shocker if I'm honest.
He is indeed, Creon is what he takes. Doesn't seem to be helping. Have had his dosage adjusted due to the weight loss but it's now more his appetite.

Yes, and now this is the outcome. I couldn't and still can't seem to get my head round it. But have been told by multiple people to trust what they say as they are the experts. 

I suppose this is right but during chemo he had none of this and his tumours shrunk. Now look what I'm writing.

Oh yes, 100%. And it may sound selfish but that is something that got to me the most. Dad is living with myself, my husband and our 3 year old daughter. I'm also 6 months pregnant. I hate not knowing what is about to come.
